column1: # The GPL-bearing components of the vendored LibreOffice tree, and the notice
# texts that cover them. The tree as a whole is MPL-2.0, but two of its parts
# are not, and both are REQUIRED by the PDF -> Office/web export targets:
#   share/xpdfimport/poppler_data     the encoding tables poppler reads
# Reachability is not theoretical. LibreOffice imports every PDF through this
# helper, and engine/office_export.py feeds a PDF straight into it for the
# docx / rtf / odt / html / xhtml targets. Measured against a copy of the tree
#   * without program/xpdfimport.exe, all five targets fail outright
#     ("source file could not be loaded"); office -> PDF conversion is
#     unaffected, which is why the exe looks removable until the export
#     still SUCCEED but silently drop the text of any PDF that draws a CJK
#     font through a predefined CMap encoding. The permissive cMap tables
#     alone do not restore it — the GPL cidToUnicode tables are the
# So neither can be trimmed, and both ship with their notices. Corresponding
# Source for the object code is the LibreOffice source release for the pinned
# version (it carries the external poppler tarball the build consumed):
# The LibreOffice 26.2.5.2 download.lst names poppler 26.06.0 and poppler-data
# 0.4.12 as the external tarballs; scripts/corresponding-source.tsv pins both.
#   * every row names a file that the provisioned tree carries
#   * a non-notice row carries a component, an SPDX expression, a source URL,
#     and the basename of a notice row that ships in the tree
#   * a sha256 is either "-" or 64 hex characters, and a pinned one must match
#   * `platform` is all, windows or linux; a gate checks the rows for its own
#     platform plus the `all` rows (bundle-libreoffice.sh reads the linux set)
